question: What are the three core things a basic computer does?

options.A: Storing drug dosages, calculating IV rates, and updating policies
options.B: Printing paper records, scanning IDs, and filing charts
options.C: Accepting data, processing it, and producing information
options.D: Connecting to the internet, sending emails, and blocking viruses

explanation: Think of a computer like a helpful assistant: it takes raw facts in, does some work on them, and gives you useful results for patient care!

question: Nursing informatics brings together which three main fields?

options.A: It requires a degree in computer engineering and clinical medicine.
options.B: It combines computer science, information science, and nursing science.
options.C: It replaces traditional bedside nursing care with automated machines.
options.D: It focuses exclusively on repairing broken hospital computer hardware.

explanation: You don't need to be a tech wizard! Nursing informatics simply blends tech tools with nursing knowledge to make patient care smoother.

question: Which of these is a classic input device you might use while giving medications?
explanation: Spot on! Input devices 'feed' information into the computer. Scanning a patient's wristband sends their details straight into the system.

question: How do output devices help you out during a busy shift?

options.A: By permanently storing backup copies of electronic health records
options.B: By allowing the nurse to manually type nursing care plans into the system
options.C: By collecting raw physiological data directly from the patient's skin
options.D: By translating processed digital data into readable sights, sounds, or printed text

explanation: Output devices take what the computer has processed and show it to you—like flashing vital signs on a screen or printing a care plan.

question: What happens to the data in your computer's RAM when you switch it off?

options.A: It is transferred to the cloud for safekeeping.
options.C: It is saved to the hard drive automatically.
options.D: It remains frozen until power is restored.

explanation: RAM has a short memory! Because it is temporary, it clears out completely the moment power goes off.

question: Why do people call the CPU the 'brain' of the computer?

options.A: It provides the physical screen display for viewing vital signs.
options.B: It processes instructions and performs calculations for running programs.
options.C: It permanently archives all patient records created in the hospital.
options.D: It connects the local hospital network to the wider internet.

explanation: Just like your brain does the thinking, the CPU does the heavy lifting by interpreting software instructions and running your apps.

question: What is the main difference between RAM and permanent storage (like an SSD)?

options.A: RAM has moving mechanical parts, while SSDs rely purely on electrical signals.
options.B: Storage is only used for input devices, while RAM is used for output devices.
options.C: Storage keeps data permanently even when powered off, while RAM loses its data.
options.D: RAM holds gigabytes of data, while storage can only hold a few kilobytes.

explanation: Think of RAM as your temporary scratchpad, and storage as your filing cabinet that keeps things safe even when the lights go out.

question: A hospital wants shock-resistant drives for mobile nursing carts that load patient charts instantly. Which one should they pick?
explanation: SSDs have no spinning parts, making them super tough for mobile carts rolling down hospital corridors and much faster than old-school hard drives!

question: Which of these best describes an operating system (OS)?

options.A: A physical input device used to scan patient identification bands
options.B: Physical memory chips that temporarily hold data while you type
options.C: Core software that manages computer hardware and provides a user interface
options.D: A specialized mobile app used exclusively for calculating medication dosages

explanation: The OS is the grand manager (like Windows or Android) that lets you talk to the computer hardware and run your favorite apps.

question: How do clinical software apps differ from system software?

options.A: Clinical apps perform specific job tasks like charting, while system software manages the computer itself.
options.B: System software is designed for patients, while clinical apps are for doctors only.
options.C: Clinical apps can only run without an operating system present.
options.D: Clinical apps are physical hardware parts, while system software is purely digital.

explanation: Clinical apps help you do your actual job (like charting vitals), while system software keeps the machine running behind the scenes.

question: What is the main goal of a computer network in a hospital?

options.A: To permanently replace the need for physical nursing assessment notes
options.B: To supply continuous electrical power during a total blackout
options.C: To increase the processing speed of the central processing unit
options.D: To connect devices so they can share information and resources

explanation: Networks link different computers together so departments can easily talk to each other and share patient updates.

question: Why is having a strong network connection so crucial for electronic health records?

options.A: It allows real-time updating and sharing of patient data across different departments.
options.B: It prevents computer hardware from overheating during heavy computational tasks.
options.C: It converts analog audio alarms into clear digital text messages.
options.D: It automatically increases the storage capacity of the local hard drive.

explanation: Real-time networking means the pharmacy, lab, and your ward see the exact same up-to-the-minute patient info instantly!

question: Which of these actions goes against basic computer safety rules in the ward?

options.A: Sharing your personal computer login password with a fellow nurse
options.B: Using a barcode scanner to verify a patient's medication before administration
options.C: Reporting a lagging computer screen to the hospital IT help desk
options.D: Logging out of the electronic health record system when leaving for lunch

explanation: Never share your password! Whatever is charted under your login account is 100% your professional responsibility.

question: Why must you always lock your computer screen when walking away from the nurses' station?

options.A: To prevent the central processing unit from overheating during idle times
options.B: To automatically save any unsaved nursing notes to the cloud
options.C: To save electrical power and extend the lifespan of the monitor display
options.D: To protect patient privacy and prevent unauthorized access to health records

explanation: Leaving a screen unlocked risks patient confidentiality. A quick lock keeps sensitive health records safe from prying eyes!
